key_insight: EEG-Xplain provides a unified way to explain black-box EEG foundation models by attributing decisions across space, time, and frequency while checking whether those explanations are reliable and physiologically plausible.
engineering_relevance: It offers a standardized interpretability layer that can improve clinical trust, model debugging, and validation of EEG foundation models such as BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba.
method: Gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based attribution across heterogeneous model architectures
Spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain explanation outputs including topographic maps, heatmaps, and spectral perturbation analysis
Population-level reliability scoring using AOPC and cross-method consistency, with LLMs generating natural-language reports
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on benchmark datasets including Mumtaz2016 and TUAB, where explanations aligned with known neurophysiological markers and also revealed some artifact/spurious-pattern dependence.
watch_item: Interpretations may still be influenced by dataset artifacts and explanation-method disagreement, so clinical use requires careful validation and consistency checks.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
